issues.body: The sequencing summary says "every reaction here is post-publication," but sections 3, 4, and 6 correctly characterize C as a producer-side check that acts before the collector publishes. The intended limitation is that A and B are post-publication and C covers only one prospective writer, not that C itself reacts after publication.
issues.fix_hint: Say that A and B react only after publication, while C acts pre-publication but constrains only the collector and cannot cover direct PUTs or other writers.
issues.title: Section 7 incorrectly calls every reaction post-publication

verdict.summary: The prior major finding is resolved: the record now consistently distinguishes the aspirational branch property from the achievable refusal/detection posture, explicitly states that A–C do not prevent publication across all write paths, and identifies the enforceable pre-write coverage that would be required. The recommendation and sequencing are sound for a findings-only design record. One minor wording inconsistency remains in section 7, but it does not undermine the corrected conclusion.
